analysis.title: Treasury Drops "At Least" From Coupon Guidance, Opening The Door To Long-End Auction Changes In 2027
key_insights: Treasury's Nov 4, 2026 refunding statement dropped "at least" from its coupon and FRN guidance. It now says it anticipates maintaining auction sizes "for the next several quarters," so the floor under current sizes is gone and every refunding is live.

Headline auction sizes were unchanged for the 11th straight refunding: $125 billion of coupons next week ($58B 3-year on Nov. 9, $42B 10-year on Nov. 10, $25B 30-year on Nov. 12), refunding about $97B of maturing paper and raising about $28B of new cash.
The 20Y stays at $16B for the November new issue and $13B for reopenings. The 30Y stays at $25B new issue and $22B reopenings.

Treasury said it "continues to evaluate potential future changes to nominal coupon and FRN auction sizes," with a focus on structural demand and the costs and risks of various issuance profiles. The article reads this as a formal review of the long end.
Treasury added a new line saying it is monitoring SOMA purchases of Treasury bills and growing private-sector demand for bills.

Treasury will convert the 7Y note from a monthly new issue to a quarterly new issue with two reopenings, like the 10Y, starting with the March 2027 new issue. This frees flexibility in the belly where increases are expected.
Buybacks stay large: up to $70B of liquidity-support purchases across buckets over the quarter, plus up to $25B in the 1-month to 2-year bucket for cash management.
Citi (Jason Williams) had predicted $3B cuts to both 20Y and 30Y auctions at this refunding, and possibly ending the 20Y. Treasury did not cut, so the call was early.

Other previews: JPMorgan (Jay Barry) expected the "next several quarters" language to stay into 2027 (wrong), Barclays (Anshul Pradhan) expected "the coming quarters" (close), and UBS (Phoebe White) said guidance was more likely than immediate action (correct).

The GS MarketStrats desk gave 65% to unchanged sizes with guidance retained and 20% to guidance softened. Goldman's rates team (William Marshall) called the outcome most closely: steady 10-30y sizes, adjusted guidance, and 2-to-7y increases beginning May 2027.
Goldman projects total nominal coupon issuance rising from $315B to $381B by late 2028, with 2s through 7s growing monthly from May 2027 and 10s, 20s and 30s frozen through the end of 2028.

TBAC recommended unchanged sizes this quarter but said coupon increases will be warranted later in FY27 (likely second half). It reported broad agreement on increases but "considerable debate" on pace and sizing at the long end, with additional issuance concentrated in 2- to 10-year sector.
TBAC said any management of Treasury's maturity profile should be done through auction sizes rather than buybacks. The article reads this as a pushback on using buybacks as a yield cap.

TBAC found no evidence that 2026 technology-related issuance crowded out long-end Treasury demand, but conceded it widened sector spreads and increased competition for long-duration capital. The article disputes this, noting Meta seeking up to €9B in a debut euro bond sale the same morning.
Dealers' median forecast implies a $2.14 trillion funding shortfall for FY2028-2029 at current coupon sizes and privately-held bill supply. The near-term gap is being filled with bills.
Treasury expects to borrow $618B in Oct-Dec and $800B in Jan-Mar, implying bill increases of $332B this quarter and $532B next quarter at constant coupons. Weekly gross bill sales just hit $626B.

Bill roadmap: current benchmark sizes held into late November with a possible short-dated CMB around month-end, reductions in December around mid-month tax receipts, and increases across the bill curve in January.

TGA is assumed at $850B at end of December and could peak at $1.025T (plus or minus $50B) in late November and late January, draining reserves while bill supply rises. The article flags possible repo and SOFR vs IORB jumpiness.
Bills are 23.0% of marketable debt versus a 22.4% historical average and the 20% TBAC advised in 2024. In Treasury's coupons-constant scenario the share rises toward 28% by 2029.

Goldman: in the Aug-Oct quarter, 20s and 30s were 11.6% of coupon dollars sold but 30.5% of rate risk, so trimming them removes a lot of duration for few dollars. Funding shorter shifts refinancing and policy-rate risk to Treasury.

2Y yields are up 111bps YTD versus 48bps for the 30Y, after a Warsh Fed hiked for the first time since 2023 in September, so shifting issuance to bills moves it to the part of the curve that repriced fastest.

Fed SOMA bill holdings rose from $195.5B to $571.5B since mid-December 2025, lifting its share of bills outstanding from 3.6% to 7.9%. That support is fading: $56B added in February versus $11B in October through Oct 28. MMF assets have leveled off and the bill market shows some price sensitivity.

The article's view: Citi was probably early, the 20Y is on borrowed time, and flat long-end sizes may be the optimistic case. The next refunding announcement is Feb 3, 2027, where "next several quarters" may be dropped too.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Headline sizes were a non-event. The change is in forward guidance, which now leaves room for future long-end adjustments.

crypto_views: Stablecoin demand, promoted by Treasury as a future bill buyer, has yet to materialize at scale.
risk_factors: Long-end auction size cuts could come in February, May or with the first increases later in 2027, which would shift supply of duration.
A bill-heavy mix raises refinancing and policy-rate risk for Treasury, and the bill market shows early price sensitivity as MMF assets level off.
Fed bill purchases are slowing just as Treasury adds about $532B of bills next quarter.
Liability-driven investor (pension) demand for long-dated Treasuries is questioned, with dealers holding mixed views.
Heavy AI-related corporate issuance competes with Treasuries for long-duration buyers.
Goldman: if higher interest costs constrain monetary policy, fiscal risk can reappear through inflation expectations and the expected policy path.
vol_and_positioning: TGA above $1 trillion twice in the next three months while bill supply ramps could make repo and SOFR fixes versus IORB jumpy, per the article and Citi's earlier warning.
30Y yields have retreated from an early-October spike to the highest since 2002 but remain well above levels from when Bessent doubled long-end buybacks in August.
geopolitical: The article refers to "pre-Iran war" levels for 30Y yields, which remain well above that level.
cross_bank_references: Citi expected 20Y and 30Y auction cuts of $3bn each on Nov 4, but Treasury did not cut.

Barclays' Anshul Pradhan suggested "the coming quarters" replace "at least the next several quarters."
UBS' Phoebe White said "guidance is more likely than immediate action."

Goldman's rates team (Marshall) called the outcome nearly exactly, expecting 2-to-7y increases from May 2027.

tension_points.bull_case: TBAC sees demand absorbing issuance well, says recent rate rises reflect strong growth and policy outlook, and Goldman expects 10s, 20s and 30s to stay frozen through 2028 with increases concentrated in 2s to 7s.
tension_points.bear_case: TBAC had considerable debate on the long end and mixed dealer views on pension demand. The article argues a cut to 20s and 30s is plausible given Treasury's discomfort with long-end yields.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The February 3, 2027 refunding announcement: if "next several quarters" is dropped or long-end sizes are cut, the frozen-long-end base case fails.

tension_points.bull_case: Treasury and Goldman note the Fed has bought bills, nearly tripling SOMA holdings, and the gap can be managed with bills near term.
tension_points.bear_case: Fed bill buying is fading ($11B in October versus $56B in February), MMF assets have leveled off, the bill market shows price sensitivity, and bills are heading toward 28% of debt by 2029 at constant coupons.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Bill supply of $532B next quarter being absorbed without price stress would weaken the bear case, while further slowing of Fed purchases would support it.

theme_stances.key_argument: A Treasury that deleted "at least" from its guidance is thinking about the supply of duration, and flat long-end sizes may be the optimistic case.
theme_stances.evidence: the supply of duration matters, not just the supply of debt

theme_stances.key_argument: Bill financing works only while someone keeps buying, and the Fed is slowing purchases as Treasury adds about half a trillion of bills next quarter.
